Attrition Outpaces Hiring by 24,000 as India's Top Six IT Firms Face Workforce Shift

30 Oct 2026, 01:37 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Careers Desk · Source: www.linkedin.com

2 min read

Data compiled by staffing firm Xpheno reveals that India's six largest IT services companies collectively recorded 92,000 employee exits over a recent one-year period while hiring only 68,000 new workers in IT and engineering functions. This dynamic resulted in a net headcount reduction of 24,422 positions, pushing the combined workforce of these industry majors down by nearly 3% to 797,722 in October 2026, compared to 822,144 in October 2025.

According to the findings, exits outpaced fresh hiring in five of the past six months. The trend highlights a broader structural adjustment within traditional technology services, where replacement hiring has slowed down significantly.

Impact on Mid-Level Roles and Traditional IT Services

Industry analysts point out that replacement hiring has been particularly low in the five to twelve years experience band. Affected categories include application maintenance, manual testing, infrastructure support, and L1 and L2 services.

Neeti Sharma, CEO of TeamLease Digital, noted that replacement hiring falls short of departures in these specific experience brackets because artificial intelligence tools are steadily reducing the requirement for repetitive, routine tasks. However, specialists emphasize that the shift is not entirely driven by automation. Francis Padamadan, CEO of Xpheno, cautioned against attributing the entire decline strictly to artificial intelligence, pointing out that conventional engineering demand remains active while companies concurrently navigate client market challenges and adjust their internal skills mix.

The Skills Mismatch and Growth Areas

While overall IT hiring has contracted by 3%, specialized domains are experiencing counter-trends. Roles tied to artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and specialized engineering continue to expand at a rate of approximately 16% year-on-year.

This divergence creates a distinct skills mismatch for professionals displaced from traditional support and maintenance functions. As enterprises pivot toward productivity gains and automated delivery models, demand increasingly favors advanced technical proficiencies over scale-driven headcount expansion.

Practical Implications and What Readers Can Verify

For technology professionals, job seekers, and market observers, the reported figures provide concrete metrics regarding the evolving nature of enterprise technology delivery.

  • What is confirmed: Combined headcount across TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra, and LTM fell by 24,422 positions over the measured timeframe due to 92,000 exits and 68,000 new hires, per Xpheno data reported by the Economic Times. Mid-level roles in manual testing, application maintenance, and infrastructure support experience lower replacement rates.
  • What remains uncertain: The exact distribution of future workforce reductions and the ultimate pace at which broader client markets will alter technology spending remain variable.
  • How to verify: Readers can review the original coverage and data summaries through the verified source link on LinkedIn: Analytics India Magazine Post.
